VBO:0200286.summary: Cães de Gado Transmontanos are calm, watchful flock guardians, reserved at first with strangers but described as responsive to gentle attention. Developed along the steep transhumance routes of Trás-os-Montes, they traditionally guard sheep and goats against wolves, often working alongside other dogs.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 368: Cão de Gado Transmontano
sources.evidence: FCI 368 documents docile, reserved, calm temperament; responsiveness to gentle handling; group flock guarding against wolves; origins in Trás-os-Montes transhumance.

VBO:0200286.shortDescription: A calm highland flock guardian, this Portuguese mastiff watches for wolves and often works alongside other dogs.

VBO:0201027.summary: Podencos Canarios are energetic, courageous rabbit hunters, using nose, sight and hearing together across broken volcanic terrain. Strongly attached to their handler, they can locate rabbits hidden in rock crevices and lava tubes.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 329: Podenco Canario
sources.evidence: FCI 329 describes courageous, dynamic, attached temperament and rabbit tracking by nose, sight and hearing through crevices, stone piles and volcanic tubes.

VBO:0201027.shortDescription: This energetic Canarian rabbit hunter combines nose, sight and hearing to search crevices and volcanic terrain.

VBO:0201402.summary: Long-haired Weimaraners share the breed’s steady, scent-driven hunting character: they search methodically, point game and work in water as well as on land. The long-haired variety has been recorded since the turn of the twentieth century, after the breed’s nineteenth-century development around Weimar and Thuringia.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 99: Weimaraner, Long-Haired
sources.evidence: FCI 99 records steady, versatile hunting temperament, systematic scent search, pointing and water work, Weimar/Thuringia roots, and a long-haired variety since around 1900.

VBO:0201402.shortDescription: A steady, methodical scent hunter, the long-haired Weimaraner points game and works on land and in water.

VBO:0201069.summary: Portuguese Pointers are affectionate, curious hunters that work persistently while keeping close contact with the hunter. Their pointing role is documented in Portugal by the fourteenth century, when the dog was known as the “podengo de mostra”; falconry and later partridge hunting also shaped its history.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 187: Portuguese Pointer
sources.evidence: FCI 187 describes kind, affectionate, curious, persistent and close-contact hunting behavior, records fourteenth-century pointing and later falconry/partridge use.

VBO:0201069.shortDescription: An affectionate, curious pointer that hunts persistently while keeping close contact with the person in the field.

VBO:0201120.summary: Rafeiros do Alentejo are calm, confident guardians traditionally entrusted with both livestock and rural estates. Often most vigilant at night, they accompanied seasonal flock movements from mountain pasture to the Alentejo plains.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 96: Rafeiro do Alentejo
sources.evidence: FCI 96 describes calm confidence, farm/estate and livestock protection, greater vigilance at night, and spread along transhumance routes into Alentejo.

VBO:0201120.shortDescription: A calm Alentejo guardian of flocks and estates, especially vigilant at night along the old transhumance routes.

VBO:0201140.summary: Romanian Carpathian Shepherd Dogs are calm, stable guardians with a strong attachment to the flock and shepherd. Selected for centuries for protection in the Carpathian mountains, they retain the agile, powerful build needed to patrol rugged grazing ground.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 350: Romanian Carpathian Shepherd Dog
sources.evidence: FCI 350 documents calm, dignified, stable temperament, attachment to herd/master, centuries of Carpathian flock defense and vigorous, agile build.

VBO:0201140.shortDescription: A calm, stable Carpathian flock guardian with strong attachment to its herd and the shepherd who tends it.

VBO:0200690.summary: Rough-haired Ibizan Podencos are nimble rabbit hunters that rely on scent and hearing to search dense cover. On their native Balearic Islands they can work together without guns: when one dog indicates game, others hang back and wait, a hunting pattern shared with the smooth-haired variety.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 89: Ibizan Podenco, Rough-Haired
sources.evidence: FCI 89 describes rabbit hunting using scent and hearing more than sight, group work, Balearic origins and the rough coat with hard dense hair and beard.

VBO:0200690.shortDescription: An alert Balearic rabbit hunter, the rough-haired Ibizan relies on scent and hearing and can work with other dogs.

VBO:0201139.summary: Romanian Bucovina Shepherds are calm, loyal flock guardians with a strong low bark used when strangers or predators approach. They traditionally patrol flock or home after dark, a working habit rooted in the transhumance country of northeastern Romania.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 357: Romanian Bucovina Shepherd
sources.evidence: FCI 357 documents calm, loyal temperament, strong low warning bark, night patrol, flock protection and Bucovina transhumance origins.

VBO:0201139.shortDescription: A calm Bucovina guardian known for low, powerful warning barks and nighttime patrols around flock or home.

VBO:0201245.summary: Slovensky Cuvacs are vigilant and courageous, with a strong attachment to the people and flocks they guard. For centuries they worked on high Slovak mountain pastures, watching livestock through harsh weather and sounding the alarm when danger approached. Their white coat helped shepherds distinguish them from predators after dark; the breed’s name also echoes its keen watchfulness.
VBO:0201245.historicalRoots: Slovak Tatra mountain guardian of livestock and pasture camps.

sources.title: FCI: Slovenský Čuvač (Standard No. 142)
sources.evidence: The standard describes loyalty, courage, vigilance and mountain guarding of livestock; white color historically helped distinguish dog from predators at night, and derives the name from hearing/watchfulness.

VBO:0201245.shortDescription: Vigilant and brave, this white Slovak mountain guardian watches flocks and stays closely attached to its people.

VBO:0201264.summary: South Russian Shepherd Dogs tend to be self-confident and independent, strongly devoted to their people but reserved with strangers. Their long shaggy coat can hide an agile worker: they guarded cattle and property across open southern steppe country. The breed took its modern name and formal shape in the early twentieth century after earlier bearded herding dogs mixed with local stock.
VBO:0201264.historicalRoots: Southern Russian steppe herding and guardian breed, standardized in the early twentieth century.

sources.title: FCI: South Russian Shepherd Dog (Standard No. 326)
sources.evidence: FCI describes balanced, self-confident independence, owner devotion and stranger aloofness; cattle and property guarding; shaggy coat hiding agility; historical development and early-1930s standard.

VBO:0201264.shortDescription: Self-confident and devoted to its people, this shaggy steppe guardian remains reserved with strangers.

VBO:0200691.summary: Smooth-haired Ibizan Podencos are agile, alert rabbit hunters that use scent and hearing to find rabbits even in dense cover. On the Balearic Islands they searched without guns, sometimes working with other dogs that waited at a distance when one found game.
VBO:0200691.historicalRoots: Balearic rabbit hunter, especially associated with Ibiza; smooth-coat variety.

sources.title: FCI: Podenco Ibicenco (Standard No. 89)
sources.evidence: FCI identifies the Balearic origin, smooth coat variety, gunless rabbit hunting using scent and hearing, cooperative waiting pattern, agile pursuit and mobile erect ears.

VBO:0200691.shortDescription: Agile and alert, this smooth-haired island hunter finds rabbits by scent and hearing, even in dense cover.

VBO:0201381.summary: Gos Rater Valencià dogs are lively and affectionate with familiar people, while keeping a watchful reserve around strangers. Valencian farms valued their quick warning bark and their persistence against rats, moles and rabbits. The breed’s rise coincided with orange growing in the region; its small working build let it move through cultivated fields and farm edges.
VBO:0201381.historicalRoots: Valencian farm ratter and alert dog associated with nineteenth-century orange-growing country.

sources.title: FCI: Gos Rater Valencià (Standard No. 370)
sources.evidence: FCI describes lively, active, affectionate and faithful behavior with reserve toward strangers, hunting of water rats, rabbits and moles, alarm barking, and association with Valencian orange cultivation.

VBO:0201381.shortDescription: Lively and affectionate with familiar people, this small Valencian farm dog warns quickly and pursues pests.

VBO:0201126.summary: Ratonero Bodeguero Andaluz dogs are curious, cheerful and bold, shaped by close work hunting rodents around Jerez wine cellars and stables. British wine traders brought Smooth Fox Terrier lines to the area, where they blended with local dogs. Their mainly white coat made them easier to spot in dim work spaces, while the breed also retained a nimble, affectionate character.
VBO:0201126.historicalRoots: Andalusian ratter of Jerez cellars and stables, with local and Smooth Fox Terrier roots.

sources.title: FCI: Ratonero Bodeguero Andaluz (Standard No. 371)
sources.evidence: FCI documents cheerful, inquisitive, affectionate, bold character; rodent work in Jerez wine cellars, stables and warehouses; British Smooth Fox Terrier ancestry; predominantly white coat selected for visibility in dark spaces.

VBO:0201126.shortDescription: Curious and bold, this Andalusian cellar dog hunted rodents around Jerez wine stores and stables.

VBO:0201338.summary: Tazy dogs are calm and self-possessed in ordinary life, then swift and keen when hunting. On Kazakhstan’s open land they have worked alone, in groups and alongside hunting birds, using both sight and scent to search for game. The breed appears in Kazakh tradition as one of the Seven Treasures, a reminder of its long connection to nomadic hunting life.
VBO:0201338.historicalRoots: Kazakh sighthound of nomadic hunting culture, used alone, in groups and with hunting birds.

sources.title: FCI: Kazakh Tazy (Standard No. 372)
sources.evidence: FCI describes balanced, calm everyday temperament and passionate agile hunting with sight and scent; solo, group and hunting-bird work; historical place in Kazakh oral tradition as one of the Seven Treasures.

VBO:0201338.shortDescription: Calm at rest and keen in the field, the Tazy hunts across Kazakhstan’s open country with sight and scent.

VBO:0201056.summary: Standard Poodles are often joyful and loyal, with a quick capacity to learn that helped them move from water work into life as companions. Their French name, caniche, recalls ducks: the breed was once used for wildfowling before its sizes and styles diversified.
VBO:0201056.historicalRoots: Largest Poodle variety; French waterfowling ancestry and later companion role.

sources.title: FCI: Poodle (Standard variety, No. 172)
sources.evidence: FCI records joyful, friendly, loyal nature and trainability; original wildfowling and caniche duck etymology; four size varieties with Standard over 45 cm; curly or corded coat and modern accepted color patterns.

VBO:0201056.shortDescription: Joyful and quick to learn, the Standard Poodle carries a waterfowling heritage into companion life.

VBO:0200054.summary: Confident and energetic, American Pit Bull Terriers are often eager to engage with people. Developed from nineteenth-century British bull-and-terrier crosses, they worked on American farms as livestock dogs and hunters; their natural agility also makes them capable climbers.
VBO:0200054.historicalRoots: Nineteenth-century bull-and-terrier ancestry; versatile American farm and livestock work.

sources.title: United Kennel Club: American Pit Bull Terrier Breed Standard
sources.evidence: UKC standard describes confidence, enthusiasm and people-oriented behavior; British bull-and-terrier origins; catch-dog, hunting and livestock uses on American farms; balanced medium athletic conformation rather than extreme muscle. UKC characteristics also document natural agility and capable climbing.

VBO:0200054.shortDescription: Confident and energetic, this agile terrier worked on American farms moving livestock and catching hogs.

VBO:0200036.summary: Confident and exuberant, American Bullies are described as gentle, friendly companions despite their powerful build. The breed emerged from American Pit Bull Terrier lines with other bull-breed influences, yet UKC recognizes it as a distinct breed and values athletic soundness over exaggeration.
VBO:0200036.shortDescription: Confident and exuberant, this powerful companion is described as gentle, friendly and athletic.
VBO:0200036.historicalRoots: Developed in the United States from American Pit Bull Terrier lines with influences from other bull breeds; recognized separately by UKC in 2013.

sources.title: UKC American Bully breed standard
sources.evidence: Characteristics describe a confident, exuberant, gentle and friendly companion; history explains its distinct development and 2013 recognition, and general appearance calls for athletic soundness.

VBO:0200172.summary: Tenacious and courageous on a hunt, Black Mouth Curs use sight, hearing and scent to locate game and have traditionally worked as family guardians too. Early American settlers relied on these all-round dogs as they moved west; their precise point of origin remains uncertain.
VBO:0200172.shortDescription: A tenacious, loyal working cur that hunts with sight, sound and scent and has a guardian tradition.
VBO:0200172.historicalRoots: An American all-round working cur used by early settlers for hunting and family guarding; exact regional origin is disputed.

sources.title: UKC Black Mouth Cur breed standard
sources.evidence: History states uncertain origin and early-settler hunting and family guarding; characteristics detail multiple senses, tenacity, courage, loyalty and protectiveness.

VBO:0201051.summary: Loyal and quick to learn, the Miniature Poodle carries the same lively, capable character described for the Poodle breed in a smaller frame. Poodles have a water-retrieving heritage; modern Miniatures can channel that alertness into training, games and other activities beyond their familiar clipped appearance.
VBO:0201051.shortDescription: Loyal and quick to learn, this smaller Poodle shares the breed’s lively character and water-dog heritage.
VBO:0201051.historicalRoots: The Miniature is a size variety of the Poodle, a European water-retrieving breed with a long companion history.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 172: Poodle
sources.evidence: FCI describes loyal character and capacity for learning, and defines the Miniature size variety as above 28 to 35 cm.

sources.title: AKC Poodle history
sources.evidence: AKC recounts the Poodle’s water-retriever ancestry, varied modern pursuits and size varieties.

VBO:0200835.summary: Serious and businesslike at work but sometimes clownish at home, the Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog has been used to track game and bay feral hogs and cattle. The breed can be independent and protective while also affectionate with familiar people; Louisiana named it the state dog in 1979.
VBO:0200835.shortDescription: Businesslike in the field and sometimes clownish at home, this Louisiana worker can be independent and loyal.
VBO:0200835.historicalRoots: A Louisiana multipurpose working dog used for game and stock; its deeper origins are uncertain, and it became Louisiana’s state dog in 1979.

sources.title: UKC Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog breed standard
sources.evidence: History notes uncertain origin, work with game and stock, and Louisiana state-dog status; characteristics describe serious work, clownish home behavior, independence and loyalty.

VBO:0201235.summary: Gentle and affectionate at home, Silken Windhounds retain the keen prey drive of a field sighthound. This modern American breed was developed from Borzoi and Whippet lines to bring a smaller, long-coated hound into the family of sporting sight hunters, while keeping its fine-boned grace and speed.
VBO:0201235.shortDescription: Gentle and devoted at home, this silky American sighthound keeps a keen eye for moving prey in the field.
VBO:0201235.historicalRoots: A modern American sighthound developed using Borzoi and Whippet lines for a smaller, long-coated sporting dog.

sources.title: UKC Silken Windhound breed standard
sources.evidence: History documents the modern breeding program and foundation lines; temperament describes strong field prey drive and gentle, affectionate devotion at home.

VBO:0201023.summary: Loyal, alert and eager to please, Plott Hounds also have a bold, fearless hunting tradition. The Plott family developed these scent hounds in the North Carolina mountains, where they tracked bears and mountain lions; their ancestors had hunted wild boar in Germany.
VBO:0201023.shortDescription: Loyal and alert with a bold hunting streak, this scent hound carries a North Carolina mountain legacy.
VBO:0201023.historicalRoots: Developed by the Plott family in North Carolina’s Appalachian region for big-game hunting.

sources.title: AKC official Plott Hound standard
sources.evidence: AKC history distinguishes ancestral German wild-boar hounds from the Plott family’s North Carolina hounds used for bear and mountain lion; UKC standard supports loyalty, alertness, eagerness to please and bold hunting character.

sources.title: AKC Plott Hound breed history
sources.evidence: AKC history distinguishes ancestral German wild-boar hounds from the Plott family’s North Carolina hounds used for bear and mountain lion; UKC standard supports loyalty, alertness, eagerness to please and bold hunting character.

VBO:0201061.summary: Loyal, lively and receptive to training, the Toy Poodle shares the Poodle’s keen learning ability despite its tiny size. Smaller Poodles became city companions in Europe, and the Toy variety was bred in the United States in the early twentieth century; its lineage still reaches back to European water dogs.
VBO:0201061.shortDescription: Tiny but lively and quick to learn, the Toy Poodle shares its larger relatives’ loyal character and water-dog roots.
VBO:0201061.historicalRoots: The smallest Poodle size variety, bred in the United States in the early twentieth century from the older European Poodle water-dog line.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 172: Poodle
sources.evidence: FCI describes loyalty and aptitude for learning and defines Toy height as above 24 to 28 cm, with a small tolerance.

sources.title: AKC Poodle history
sources.evidence: AKC describes the Toy variety’s city-companion development and Poodle water-retrieving roots.

VBO:0201340.summary: Lively, alert and affectionate, the Teddy Roosevelt Terrier has a strong ratting and farm-work inheritance. The low-set, short-legged terrier is curious and often eager to join familiar people’s activities; historically it was known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier before adopting its present name.
VBO:0201340.shortDescription: Lively, affectionate and curious, this short-legged farm terrier has a long tradition of ratting work.
VBO:0201340.historicalRoots: An American short-legged ratting and farm terrier related to the Rat Terrier and formerly known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier.

sources.title: AKC official Teddy Roosevelt Terrier standard
sources.evidence: History covers ratting/farm work and former names; temperament describes kindness, intelligence, lively alertness, affection and curiosity.

VBO:0200178.summary: Alert and affectionate, the Blue Gascony Griffon is an energetic French scent hound with a fine nose and a strong voice. Traditionally it worked hare and could track wild boar; its rough-coated Pyrenean line arose from a Gascony Blue hound crossed with a griffon, then underwent a revival after becoming scarce.
VBO:0200178.shortDescription: Alert and affectionate with a fine nose and strong voice, this rough-coated hound has Pyrenean hunting roots.
VBO:0200178.historicalRoots: An old Pyrenean French scent hound from a medium Gascony Blue crossed with a griffon; revived after near disappearance from organized dog fancy.

sources.title: FCI standard No. 32: Blue Gascony Griffon
sources.evidence: FCI documents Pyrenean roots, Gascony Blue–griffon crossing and revival, hare and boar work, fine nose, good voice, alert energy and affection.
